prompt:
A ${{mass}}\text{ kg}$ crate is pulled across a level floor by a horizontal force of ${{force}}\text{ N}$. The coefficient of kinetic friction is $\mu_k={{mu}}$.

Use $F_f=\mu_k mg$ and $\sum F=ma$ to find the crate's acceleration. Show your work and include units.
teacher_notes: Good for testing free-response spacing and rubric display later.
explanation: The friction force is $F_f=\mu_kmg=({{mu}})({{mass}})(9.8)\approx{{calc: round(mu * mass * 9.8, 1)}}\text{ N}$. The net force is ${{force}}-{{calc: round(mu * mass * 9.8, 1)}}={{calc: round(force - mu * mass * 9.8, 1)}}\text{ N}$, so $a=\frac{F_{net}}{m}=\frac{{{calc: round(force - mu * mass * 9.8, 1)}}}{{{mass}}}\approx{{calc: round((force - mu * mass * 9.8) / mass, 1)}}\text{ m/s}^2$.

rubric.criterion: Reports acceleration with units and reasonable rounding

sample_solution: $F_f=({{mu}})({{mass}}\text{ kg})(9.8\text{ m/s}^2)={{calc: round(mu * mass * 9.8, 1)}}\text{ N}$. $F_{net}={{force}}-{{calc: round(mu * mass * 9.8, 1)}}={{calc: round(force - mu * mass * 9.8, 1)}}\text{ N}$. $a=F_{net}/m={{calc: round(force - mu * mass * 9.8, 1)}}/{{mass}}={{calc: round((force - mu * mass * 9.8) / mass, 2)}}\text{ m/s}^2$.
exemplar_answer: The normal force is $mg$, so kinetic friction is about ${{calc: round(mu * mass * 9.8, 1)}}\text{ N}$. The applied force is larger than friction, leaving a net force of about ${{calc: round(force - mu * mass * 9.8, 1)}}\text{ N}$. Dividing by ${{mass}}\text{ kg}$ gives $a\approx{{calc: round((force - mu * mass * 9.8) / mass, 1)}}\text{ m/s}^2$ in the direction of the pull.
